parameters.content:
## Book jobs in Google Calendar from accepted quotes in Google Sheets

For service businesses that track quotes in Google Sheets and jobs in Google Calendar.

### How it works
1. You set a quote's `status` to `accepted` in the sheet. Within 15 minutes the customer gets a personal booking link.
2. The customer books one of the free times in your calendar. The job goes to Google Calendar and the row to `scheduled`.
3. Every morning, customers with a job tomorrow get a reminder.

To change a date, move the event in Calendar and update `job_start`. The reminder reads the sheet.

### Setup
1. Use the sheet described in the **Sheet** note.
2. Pick your Google credential in each Google node.
3. Paste your sheet URL in **Document** in all six Google Sheets nodes: Find accepted quotes, Mark link sent, Find the quote, Read the row again, Mark scheduled, Find scheduled jobs.
4. Edit **Settings**. Set Workflow settings > Timezone to the zone in `timezone`.
5. Open **Booking form**, copy its **Production URL** (it ends in `/form/book-job`) and paste it in **Settings** > `booking_form_url`. Then activate.
6. Test: add a row with your own email, set `status` to `accepted` and wait up to 15 minutes. Do not share the Booking form URL: each customer gets a personal link by email.

If nothing happens, check **Executions**.

### Requirements
- Google Sheets, Calendar and Gmail credentials in n8n: docs.n8n.io/integrations/builtin/credentials/google/. If your Google Cloud app is External and in Testing, the connection expires after 7 days; publish it to avoid this.
- The form path `book-job` must be free. Change it in **Booking form** if another workflow uses it.

Our paid template follows up Gmail quotes and tells you when the customer says yes: https://payhip.com/b/OyN5V

One person is behind Small Hours. AI agents built and tested this template.

### Sheet: tab named `Requests`
Same sheet as the quote request template. To create it, paste this line in cell A1, then Data > Split text to columns:
`request_id,received_at,status,name,email,phone,service,address,preferred_date,details,missing_fields,quote_id,quote_amount,thread_id,quote_sent_at,follow_ups_sent,last_follow_up_at,reply_label,job_start,event_id,closed_at`

Needed in each row: `request_id` (any unique text, like R-001), `name`, `email`. Statuses, in lowercase: `accepted` (you set it), `booking_sent`, `scheduled`.

### Settings
`owner_email`: told when no times are free; change it first. `work_days`: 1 = Monday ... 7 = Sunday. `day_start`, `day_end`: 24h. `job_hours`: job length and time block. `min_notice_hours`, `days_ahead`, `max_options`: earliest booking, how far ahead, how many times shown. `timezone`: like America/Chicago, not EST.

## 1. Set your details
Your business name, your email, your working days and how long a job takes.

## 2. It wakes up three ways
Every 15 minutes for accepted quotes, when a customer opens a link, and every morning for reminders.

parameters.content:
## 3. Accepted quotes get a booking link
Rows set to accepted move to booking_sent and the customer gets an email with a personal link.

nodes.name: Section: Accepted quotes get a booking link

parameters.content:
## 4. The customer sees only your free times
Free times come from your main calendar. Any event there blocks that time, unless it is marked Free.

nodes.name: Section: The customer sees only your free times

parameters.content:
## 5. It checks again and books the job
Calendar and row are read once more right before booking, so a time is not booked twice.

nodes.name: Section: It checks again and books the job

parameters.content:
## 6. The row and the customer are updated
The row moves to scheduled and the customer gets a confirmation.

nodes.name: Section: The row and the customer are updated

parameters.content:
## 7. You are told when it cannot book
A used link or a time just taken shows the customer a page. No free times, or a link that could not be sent, also sends you an email.

Every morning at 8:00, customers with a job tomorrow get an email.
